archetype.name: Pocket Passer (accuracy-first)
archetype.definition: A 36-year-old who wins from the pocket with timing and ball placement at 10-plus yards, adds almost nothing with his legs, and pays for his patience in sacks.

report.headline: Seattle-era accuracy is back; the sacks and tough defenses still cap him
report.take:
Geno Smith's 2026 looks far more like his Seattle seasons than last year's Raiders season. His EPA per dropback of 0.074 sits right in the 0.071-0.085 band he posted from 2022 to 2024, after a -0.1 in 2025. His CPOE of 3.72 (12th of 55) is back near his Seattle norm after a 0.7 last year. The interceptions have nearly disappeared: a 1% rate, 10th best, after 17 picks last season ranked dead last. He is no longer the runner of 2022. At 36 he has 58 rushing yards, and his designed runs are an EPA sink. He is a pocket thrower now, plain and simple.

The value lives downfield. On throws of 10-plus air yards he is at 0.61 EPA per attempt with an 11.7 CPOE. Under 10 yards he is at 0.064. The 64 throws behind the line, mostly screens and dump-offs, lose EPA as a group. This is not a gunslinger profile, though. His aggressiveness is down 2 points from last year and his intended air yards (7.9) are modest. He picks his shots, and when he takes one it is usually there. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell carry the target tree at roughly 0.24 EPA per target each. The tight ends and backs are where drives go to die.

Two things are hidden in the averages. The first is sacks. His sack rate of 8.7% ranks 37th, and 14 of his 30 sacks came on third down, where he faces an average of 8.1 yards to go and converts a third of the time. His time to throw is up to 2.92, and the line ranks 24th in hit rate allowed. So the sacks are partly protection and partly a veteran waiting for the downfield window. Career pressure-to-sack rates of 22% to 46% suggest it swings with his surroundings.

The second is opponent quality, which drives his game log more than anything. Against defenses now ranked in the bottom ten (Tennessee, Detroit, Miami, Las Vegas, the Chargers) he posted strongly positive EPA every time. Against Chicago, Cleveland, Kansas City and Buffalo he went negative, sometimes sharply. The last three games (-0.014 EPA per dropback) look like a slump. Really they are two strong defenses, one of them a game where he played only 48% of snaps, followed by a sharp 17-of-21, three-touchdown day against a soft Chargers unit.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep placement
strengths.body: His 10-plus-yard throws produce more than the rest of his passing combined. The CPOE behind that is double digits, so this is accuracy, not just volume of shots. The skill is real and consistent with his Seattle peak. A 15.4 CPOE on 36 deep attempts will cool, though, so expect good rather than absurd.

strengths.title: Accuracy back to career norm
strengths.body: A 3.72 CPOE ranks 12th and sits 5.3 points over the league average. That lines up with his 2022-2024 levels, which makes last year's 0.7 look like the outlier. Accuracy has held up across seasons, so it should stay.

strengths.title: Interceptions way down
strengths.body: A 1% interception rate after a league-worst 17 picks in 2025 is the biggest single swing in his profile. He is being less aggressive, and his turnover-worthy interception count matches his actual picks, so it isn't pure luck. Still, he has thrown 9 to 17 interceptions in every full season. Some climb back toward his norm is likely.

concerns.title: Sacks and third-and-long drag
concerns.body: His 8.7% sack rate ranks 37th, and nearly half of his sacks came on third down, where his EPA turns negative. Part of this is the cost of holding for downfield windows: his time to throw is up from last year. Part is a line that ranks 24th in hit rate allowed. It is structural and likely persists, though weaker pass rushes soften it.

concerns.title: Good defenses shut him down
concerns.body: Against Chicago, Cleveland, Kansas City and Buffalo, the passing EPA went negative and bad-throw rates spiked. Without mobility to escape structure, he needs clean timing. Top defenses take that away, and the Jets' run-leaning approach gives him little volume to work through it.

concerns.title: Red-zone efficiency lags
concerns.body: He has 10 red-zone touchdowns, but those plays carry negative EPA overall, with a 53.5% completion rate and 7 sacks inside the 20. A compressed field takes away his intermediate strength. This is closer to a real limitation than noise, though the touchdown count itself is fine.

trend.note: His weekly line tracks the opponent's defense more than any form curve. Strong games came against Detroit, Miami, Las Vegas and the Chargers, and he cratered against Kansas City and Buffalo. The last-five window (0.105 EPA per dropback) is actually above his season mark.

nextGame.headline: Soft Miami pass defense and a weak rush suit him
nextGame.body:
Miami is close to an ideal matchup. It ranks 27th in pass defense EPA, 26th in sack rate, and 26th against deep throws, giving up 0.633 EPA per deep play. Its two biggest strengths would be pressure and a stingy deep game, and it has neither. That takes away the sack problem and feeds his best throws. He already beat this defense in Week 7 at home: 23 of 30, three touchdowns, 9.5 EPA. The Book has the Jets as 3.5-point road favorites, but the total is only 40.5. Miami's offense ranks 28th in EPA and runs far more than expected, which points to a shorter, lower-volume game. Expect efficiency, not a big attempt count.

Availability cuts both ways. Miami is without quarterback Malik Willis (IR), which drags its offense down further and lowers the chance of a shootout. Starting corner JuJu Brents (70% of snaps) is questionable with a shoulder injury, and his absence would thin a secondary that is already leaky. On the Jets' side, wide receivers Isaiah Williams (57% of snaps) and Omar Cooper Jr. (53%) are both out. That narrows the passing game to Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and the tight ends. The forecast is early and shows modest wind with a chance of drizzle, nothing yet that should change the passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield shots against a leaky deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His 10-plus-yard throws are the engine of his season. Miami ranks 26th in deep EPA allowed, and its 26th-ranked sack rate means he should get time to wait on those windows. This is where most of his value should come from.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends against Miami's weak spot
keyMatchups.body: Miami ranks last in EPA allowed to opposing top tight ends and sees an above-league share of targets go to the position. With two receivers out, more volume should flow to the tight ends. That helps only if it goes to Mason Taylor, who has been productive, rather than Kenyon Sadiq, who has been flat.

keyMatchups.title: Wilson against a stingy WR1 matchup
keyMatchups.body: Miami has held opposing No. 1 receivers well under their averages in fantasy terms. The per-play EPA it allows that role is poor, though, so Wilson's efficiency should hold even if his volume dips. Brents' status matters here.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Jets let him throw intermediate and deep early, or sit on a lead against a Willis-less Miami and cap his attempts.

restOfSeason.body:
The core of this season is sustainable because it matches who he was from 2022 to 2024. He is an accurate, timing-based pocket passer who wins between 10 and 20 yards and adds positive EPA per dropback. What should regress is the extremes. A 15-plus CPOE on deep throws will cool. The interception rate will likely drift up toward his career norm as volume accumulates. The sacks are unlikely to improve much behind this line with his time to throw creeping up.

Volume is the ceiling. The Jets run more than expected, and he is averaging under 30 attempts. With a bottom-five defense he will sometimes chase, but his trailing-big sample is small. Expect weekly output of roughly 200-240 passing yards with 1.1-1.7 touchdowns, a few strong games against soft defenses, and quiet ones against good units. Rushing adds nothing.
swingFactors: Health of the Jets' receiver depth

confidence.note: 11 starts and a profile matching his 2022-24 seasons, but deep splits are small and results swing with opponents.
